reason: Wires the note tier's store into the running app, so <notes> can stop being structurally empty. Three pieces: a [notes] config section (nora/config.py, config.example.toml) whose only field is enabled, defaulting FALSE - the tier stays dormant until an operator turns it on, and there is deliberately no render cap because spec 5.1 makes the index uncapped (a note missing from it is invisible, and invisible is indistinguishable from absent); construction in nora/app/composition.py, SqlNoteStore(engine) when enabled and None when not, gated on its own flag rather than [language]'s because this tier is not the Dreamer's; and the read itself, TranscriptInjection._notes, joined to the existing concurrent wave. Two properties are load-bearing: the read is scoped by WORKSPACE (Conversation.workspace, DEC-105/spec 3) and not by conversation - the only read in that assembler that is not room-keyed, said so in the method docstring because every neighbour keys on the room - and it fails SOFT like its siblings, answering () and counting nora_errors_total{stage="notes"} rather than raising, since an uncaught exception there would cancel three sibling reads in the gather and kill a turn that would otherwise have worked. A room the policy cannot name is treated as a wiring gap: no read at all rather than a guessed workspace, counted so it cannot go missing silently. The eighth leaf read joins the SECOND inner gather rather than adding a third branch, keeping both branches at four and inside asyncio.gather's distinctly-typed overloads - a flat eight would join every return type down to object under mypy. Still nothing WRITES a note (no tools, no curator), so turning the flag on today buys a SELECT that returns nothing: no user-observable change.
